newsitem.title: UK: British army makes safe bomb near Irish border.
newsitem.headline: British army makes safe bomb near Irish border.

text.p: Police in Northern Ireland said on Sunday that British army experts had made safe a bomb found near a village on the border with the Republic of Ireland.
"A device with 250 pounds (110 kg) of homemade explosives has been made safe," a police spokesman said. "It is thought it might have been there for some time."
A four-day operation began on Thursday when a joint army-police patrol found oil drums with wires leading from them and bomb-making equipment in a derelict building near the village of Cullyhanna.

The discovery came after the Irish Republican Army (IRA), fighting to oust Britain from Northern Ireland, planted a huge bomb at Belfast Castle on New Year's Eve. Police said that 1,000 pound (480 kg) bomb had been designed for "mass murder".
The IRA ended a 17-month ceasefire last February when it exploded a bomb that killed two people in London's Docklands district.
Northern Ireland's stalled peace process seemed further jeopardised on Sunday as pro-British Loyalist guerrillas threatened to end their own two-year truce and retaliate against IRA attacks.
A "senior Loyalist source" told the Irish Times that if the latest IRA campaign killed anyone, Loyalists would avenge the attack "big time".
